answer_1.quote: XSTEST can be used to test any generative language model.
answer_1.outputs: Model responses to safe and unsafe prompts categorized as full compliance, full refusal, or partial refusal.

answer_2.quote: However, we explore two automated evaluation methods as more efficient alternatives... First, we use a simple string-match method... Second, we use GPT-4... to classify responses...

answer_3.quote: Second, we use GPT-4, prompted with the taxonomy laid out in §4.2, to classify responses as full compliance, full refusal, or partial refusal, in a zero-shot setup.
methods: zero-shot classification with a prompt defining response types

answer_4.quote: We evaluate all models by manually annotating their responses on XSTEST. All annotations were completed by three authors of this paper...
answer_4.guideline: Differentiate between three primary types of responses: full compliance, full refusal, or partial refusal.
